heading: Vermont Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Vermont paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Vermont income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable Child Care Contribution deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Vermont uses progressive income tax withholding and has an additional payroll contribution supporting childcare services. Understanding these deductions can help you compare employment opportunities and manage monthly expenses.

Whether you work in Burlington, Montpelier, Rutland, South Burlington or another Vermont community, this calculator can help you understand your earnings.

## How to Use the Vermont Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross compensation before taxes and deductions.

Select your payment frequency. Enter federal and Vermont income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include applicable benefit deductions. If an employee Child Care Contribution was withheld, enter the amount under Benefits in Advanced settings, under Other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual taxes and remaining take-home income.

For greater accuracy, use your latest payroll statement and withholding certificates.

## Vermont Payroll Taxes in 2026

Your actual paycheck depends on taxable wages, withholding elections, employer arrangements and employee benefits.

Visit the [Vermont Department of Taxes](https://tax.vermont.gov/) for official state tax information.

## How Vermont State Income Tax Works

Vermont uses a progressive individual income tax system.

The applicable employer percentage schedules for 2026 contain four marginal withholding rates:

- 3.35%.
- 6.60%.
- 7.60%.
- 8.75%.

The state also provides zero-withholding ranges based on applicable adjusted wages and withholding classification.

Employers subtract withholding allowances before applying the appropriate payroll-period percentage table.

Read the official [2026 Vermont Income Tax Withholding Instructions](https://tax.vermont.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/GB-1210-2026.pdf) for the calculation methodology.

## Vermont Biweekly Withholding Tables

The 2026 biweekly percentage method for the single withholding classification uses the following adjusted wage thresholds.

Married employees use a separate schedule with different thresholds.

These are employer withholding tables rather than annual individual income tax return brackets.

The complete [Vermont 2026 percentage-method tables](https://tax.vermont.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/TaxTables-2026.pdf) cover the applicable payroll frequencies.

## Understanding Vermont Form W-4VT

Vermont employees are encouraged to complete Form W-4VT to provide state-specific withholding information to their employers.

Each ordinary withholding allowance has an annual value of $5,400 in 2026.

Employees with multiple jobs or working spouses should review their allowance selections carefully to avoid insufficient withholding.

The [Vermont employee withholding guidance](https://tax.vermont.gov/individuals/personal-income-tax/withholding) explains how to determine appropriate withholding allowances.

Download the official [Form W-4VT](https://tax.vermont.gov/content/form-w-4vt) and review the [withholding certificate FAQs](https://tax.vermont.gov/individuals/personal-income-tax/withholding/faqs) for additional information.

## How to Calculate Vermont Income Tax Withholding

Suppose you receive $2,500 in Vermont taxable wages every two weeks and claim one applicable withholding allowance using the single classification.

Subtract the biweekly allowance:

$2,500 − $207.69 = $2,292.31.

The adjusted wages fall into the applicable 6.60% bracket.

Vermont withholding:

$65.39 + (($2,292.31 − $2,103) × 6.60%).

Estimated state withholding: $77.88 before any additional requested withholding.

Your employer's authorized calculation and rounding method may produce a slightly different result.

## Vermont Child Care Contribution

Vermont introduced its Child Care Contribution on July 1, 2024.

The contribution supports childcare and early childhood education programs.

The total employer payroll tax rate is 0.44% of covered wages.

Employers may recover up to one-quarter of that contribution from employee wages.

This means the maximum ordinary employee contribution rate is 0.11%.

Employers may choose to pay the entire contribution instead of deducting any portion from employees.

Review the official [Vermont Child Care Contribution guidance](https://tax.vermont.gov/business/child-care-contribution) and [Vermont contribution legislation](https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/32/246/10553) for additional information.

## Does Vermont Child Care Contribution Have a Wage Ceiling?

The Child Care Contribution is not subject to the ordinary Social Security annual wage ceiling.

Eligible wages can therefore continue attracting this contribution even after an employee reaches the annual Social Security taxable wage limit.

A paycheck calculator should maintain separate wage bases for Social Security, Medicare, Vermont income tax and the Child Care Contribution.

The official [Vermont Child Care Contribution guide](https://tax.vermont.gov/sites/tax/files/documents/GB-1326.pdf) explains applicable covered wages and employer responsibilities.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Vermont Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

Employers follow [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) when calculating ordinary federal withholding.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages up to $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare applies at 1.45% of covered earnings, while additional Medicare withholding may apply above the employer's $200,000 annual threshold.

Review [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and the [Social Security Administration wage base information](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html) for official contribution rules.

## Vermont Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually and receiving 26 biweekly payments.

Assume ordinary single federal withholding settings, one Vermont withholding allowance and the maximum ordinary employee Child Care Contribution.

This example assumes no employee benefit deductions or reached federal payroll contribution thresholds.

If your employer pays the entire Child Care Contribution, your take-home pay would increase by $2.75 under otherwise identical assumptions.

## Vermont Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose an employee earns $27 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $1,080.

Overtime earnings: $243.

Total gross earnings: $1,323.

Assuming all wages are covered and the maximum ordinary employee childcare contribution applies, the deduction would be approximately $1.46.

Applicable federal and Vermont income taxes would also reduce the paycheck.

Consult the [Vermont Department of Labor](https://labor.vermont.gov/) and [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable employment requirements.

## Working in Vermont and Living in New Hampshire

Employees living in New Hampshire while working in Vermont may owe Vermont income tax on qualifying Vermont-sourced employment earnings.

New Hampshire's absence of a personal wage income tax does not automatically exempt Vermont employment income.

Remote work and employment across multiple states may require separate income allocation calculations.

Review the [Vermont withholding guidance](https://tax.vermont.gov/individuals/calculating-withholding) before applying a nonresident exemption.

## Managing Your Vermont Take-Home Income

Build your [household budget](/calculators/budget-calculator/) using estimated net earnings rather than annual gross salary.

Include housing, groceries, transportation, healthcare, utilities and required debt payments.

Vermont households may also benefit from budgeting for seasonal heating and winter transportation expenses.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a suitable savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare compensation arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Vermont's income tax rate in 2026?

Vermont's ordinary employer withholding schedules use rates of 3.35%, 6.60%, 7.60% and 8.75%. The amount deducted depends on applicable wages, withholding classification and allowances.

### How much is Vermont's Child Care Contribution for employees?

Employers may deduct up to 0.11% of covered employee wages. They may also choose to pay the entire contribution themselves.

### Does Vermont's childcare payroll contribution stop at the Social Security wage ceiling?

No. The Child Care Contribution does not use the ordinary Social Security annual wage ceiling.
